title: Red Dead Redemption 2
provenance: tested locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r5, 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-11: Vulkan under two MoltenVK builds, DirectX 12 under D3DMetal and the DX11 setting all fail before the first frame. Status stays community because there is no verdict for a title we tested and could not run.
notes: Does not run on this Mac as of 2026-09-10 (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r5), and both of its renderers now have a precise, reproducible failure. VULKAN (the game's default): the Rockstar launcher signs in, RDR2 opens a 1280x720 window, loads to 98 per cent, creates its swapchain and exits without a frame, because MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses 'vkCreateImage(): If tiling is VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR, mipLevels must be 1' (3) and 'imageType must be VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D' (16), with MoltenVK's shader translator also emitting uncompilable Metal (gl_CullDistance in an undeclared struct member) and about 10900 AGX bytes_per_row assertions along the way. Identical on every run. DIRECTX 12 can be selected and reached, which took the whole evening to establish: there is no -dx12 switch (the exe knows -vulkan, -ignoreDifferentVideoCard, -safemode, -ignorepipelinecache); the API is set only in Documents/Rockstar Games/Red Dead Redemption 2/Settings/system.xml, as <API>kSettingAPI_DX12</API> inside the <advancedGraphics> block, in a complete file (root rage__fwuiSystemSettingsCollection, version 37, configSource kSettingsConfig_Safe, taken from files the game wrote on Windows). With that file the game does load d3d12.dll, but the Rockstar launcher needs DXMT's Direct3D 11 (it loads d3d11/d3d10core/dxgi only from system32, never from its own folder) while the game needs a D3D12 provider, and one process tree has one search path. The configuration that gives both what they need: graphics mode DXMT, and on the Steam program a WINEDLLPATH_PREPEND listing the dxmt and d9vk directories first and the d3dmetal directory after them, so d3d11 resolves to DXMT for the launcher and d3d12, which DXMT does not ship, falls through to D3DMetal for the game, plus CX_D3DMETALPATH and the DYLD fallback paths pointing at D3DMetal's external folder. Under that, the launcher signs in, RDR2 initialises D3DMetal (the framework, its IR converter and winemetal all load into RDR2.exe) and for the first time creates no Vulkan swapchain and logs no MoltenVK error at all. It then dies about 30 seconds in: D3DMetal answers a Direct3D 12 call with 'err: Not implemented', and the game faults on an execute access to 0x20019008070c10, a garbage function pointer, the same address with and without Highball's timestamp shim, so the shim is not the cause and the missing call is inside Apple's Game Porting Toolkit. Winedbg gives no backtrace. Which D3D12 method is unimplemented is the one open question, and a stub for it in the timestamp shim (which already patches D3DMetal vtable slots) is the plausible fix, if it can be identified. Vulkan cannot be removed to force anything: RDR2.exe hard-imports ffx_fsr2_api_vk_x64.dll, which hard-imports vulkan-1.dll. Disabling amd_ags_x64 kills the process outright (RDR2.exe imports it statically), unlike Guardians of the Galaxy. 2026-09-11, two more routes closed. A CrossOver community guide sets <API>kSettingAPI_DX11</API>: the value exists in the exe's enum but RDR2 on PC has no Direct3D 11 renderer, so the game reads it and falls back to Vulkan (same 16 linear-3D refusals, Rockstar's crash detection reports 0xc0000005 after about 20 seconds), which means the guide's author was running on CrossOver 25's Vulkan, that is CodeWeavers' MoltenVK 1.2.10 fork rather than upstream 1.4.1. The engine carries that fork unused at frameworks/moltenvkcx, and win32u.so opens libMoltenVK.dylib by bare name, so DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at that folder swaps it in with nothing else changed. Under 1.2.10 the game gets further than under any other configuration: the linear-3D refusals do not appear until late, the load bar reaches 84 per cent at a steady 60 fps HUD, and then the game shows its own ERR_GFX_D3D_DEFERRED_MEM 'Out of memory' dialog, because that MoltenVK refuses 'vkAllocateMemory(): Host-coherent VkDeviceMemory objects cannot be associated with optimal-tiling images' 1729 times (a macOS-only restriction upstream dropped for Apple Silicon by 1.4) and 'does not support rendering to linear images' 144 times. So each MoltenVK build blocks the Vulkan path in a different place, and a build that does neither would be the fix: upstream 1.4.1 minus its linear-3D refusal, or the 1.2.10 fork minus its host-coherent refusal. On an M4 Pro the guide's author reports success with the same 1.2.10, so the memory-type selection may also differ by GPU family.

knownIssues.symptom: On its default Vulkan renderer: loads to about 98 per cent, opens a window, exits without a frame. On DirectX 12 (selectable only through system.xml): D3DMetal initialises, then the game crashes about 30 seconds in.
knownIssues.cause: Vulkan: MoltenVK 1.4.1 refuses the game's linear-tiled mipmapped images. DirectX 12: Apple's D3DMetal answers a D3D12 call the game needs with 'Not implemented' and the game calls through the result (execute fault at 0x20019008070c10).
knownIssues.fix: none today. Both are engine work: a MoltenVK change, or identifying and stubbing the unimplemented D3D12 call in the timestamp shim that already fronts D3DMetal.

knownIssues.symptom: With CodeWeavers' MoltenVK 1.2.10 fork (the CrossOver 25 build) in place of upstream 1.4.1: loads to 84 per cent, then the game's own 'ERR_GFX_D3D_DEFERRED_MEM: Out of memory' dialog.
knownIssues.cause: That MoltenVK refuses host-coherent memory for optimal-tiling images 1729 times and rendering to linear images 144 times, so the game's deferred allocator runs dry. Setting <API>kSettingAPI_DX11</API> as some guides suggest changes nothing: RDR2 has no D3D11 renderer and falls back to Vulkan.
knownIssues.fix: none today. Needs a MoltenVK that accepts both the linear-3D images (which 1.2.10 tolerates longer than 1.4.1) and host-coherent optimal images (which 1.4.1 accepts and 1.2.10 refuses).
